propositions: The janitor discovery rubric covers test smelliness and change-detector health but does not check whether test assertions can fail when their guarded contracts are violated, leaving oracle-strength gaps undetected.
Two bugs escaped to production in Aug 2026 (0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e, 9bb7-4430-1202-4d93) because assertions that should have caught contract violations passed silently (fail-open oracle pattern).
Concern #12 must be added to discovery.md to systematize oracle-strength review using the existing antipattern vocabulary from code-review-tests.md, sharded by test-tree region like concern #11.

The portable fallback in references/patterns.md must define oracle strength independently for non-rebar repos lacking the code-review-tests.md rubric, including three antipattern ids verified absent from the rubric.

The schema at discovery.md:152 hardcodes 'eleven concerns' while twelve will exist after the change, creating a silent drift that no test fails on; a new durable test derives the count from both sides and asserts agreement.

Verification must anchor test-only findings on the guarded production contract rather than file path, and demand tree-state proof (escape_input or deliberate-breakage run) demonstrating harm reachability.
